title: The Seventh Voyage of Sindbad (हिन्दी)
summary: Sindbad concluded his adventures with the seventh and final voyage: [HI]
full_text:
Sindbad concluded his adventures with the seventh and final voyage:

'The Caliph Harun al-Rashid summoned me and requested that I undertake a royal embassy to return gifts to the King of Serendib. I fulfilled the mission with honor, but upon the return voyage, our ship was attacked by corsairs. I was sold into slavery to an ivory merchant in a distant coastal kingdom.

My master gave me a bow and arrows, placed me in a high tree in the jungle, and commanded me to shoot wild elephants for their ivory tusks.

One morning, an immense herd of hundreds of elephants surrounded my tree! The largest bull, a colossal beast with tusks of gleaming white, wrapped his trunk around the trunk of the tree, uprooted it with a single heave, and threw it to the ground.

The great bull lifted me gently in his trunk, placed me upon his broad back, and carried me through the jungle to the summit of a forested hill.

There, to my absolute amazement, the bull deposited me amidst a vast plain covered with thousands of bleached elephant skeletons and mountains of ancient ivory tusks! The wise beast had shown me the natural cemetery of his ancestors, teaching me: 'Take the ivory of the dead, and cease to slay the living!'

I ran back to my master and revealed the secret graveyard. Overjoyed, the merchant granted me my freedom, shared the ivory treasure with me, and loaded a ship for Baghdad.

I returned home, threw myself before the Caliph, and vowed never to tempt the seas again. I have spent my remaining years in peace, using my treasures to build orphanages, feed the hungry, and welcome travelers like you, O Hindbad!'

Hindbad embraced the great sailor, thanked him for the lesson in fortitude, and lived beside him in lifelong friendship.
moral: True completion of life's journey arrives when adventure yields to wisdom, peace, and boundless charity. [HI]
